file: papers/pdf/Brownell et al - 2024 - Choice or Chance - How Successful Entrepreneurs Talk About Luck.pdf
about: A qualitative study of 70 How I Built This podcast interviews examining how successful entrepreneurs talk about luck in their success, finding luck is perceived as a combination of structural advantages (timing, privilege, people), openness (awareness, self-efficacy), and seizing opportunities (agency, perseverance).

candidates.label: Luck vs serendipity distinction
candidates.definition: Pure luck is chance outside one's control, whereas serendipity involves human intervention, defined as intentional search leading to unintended discovery.
candidates.applies_when: An account describes an unexpected discovery that arose while the person was actively searching or acting, rather than a purely external chance event.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The event happened entirely outside the person's control with no search or intervention (pure luck, e.g., birthplace, a pandemic).

candidates.label: Luck that happened to me
candidates.definition: Luck as a function of structural, external, objective factors that the entrepreneur discovered rather than made.
candidates.applies_when: The person attributes success to external circumstances they did not cause, such as market conditions, birth, or who came along.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The person says they made their own luck through their awareness, belief or action.

candidates.label: Luck I made myself
candidates.definition: Luck as a function of agentic, internal factors: being aware, believing in oneself, acting and persisting; entrepreneurs often hold both views at once.
candidates.applies_when: The person uses phrases like 'you make your own luck' or credits luck to their own alertness, belief or action.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Luck is described as wholly given by circumstances.

candidates.label: Right place, right time
candidates.definition: Beneficial timing in which the market or environment was ready for the venture at the moment the entrepreneur launched it; a window before which it was too early and after which too late.
candidates.applies_when: The account credits a favorable moment, trend, or market shift (e.g., post-crisis consumer mood, natural foods wave) for the venture's take-off.

candidates.label: Right people at right time
candidates.definition: Chance arrival of or connection with key people—team members, partners, earlier acquaintances—who shaped the venture.
candidates.applies_when: The person describes people coming into their life unexpectedly at a crucial time, or prior contacts resurfacing to help the venture.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The person describes deliberately hiring or recruiting through planned processes without any sense of chance.

candidates.label: Privilege
candidates.definition: Advantages of birth, family, education, health, and financial support that entrepreneurs regard as luck and that enabled them to recognize and act on opportunities.
candidates.applies_when: The account credits supportive parents, birthplace, debt-free education, financial cushion, or early access (e.g., a computer at home) as enabling the venture.

candidates.label: Social and relational capital
candidates.definition: Networks and relationships available before and during venture creation that provide otherwise unavailable resources and are perceived as luck.
candidates.applies_when: The person attributes venture progress to their network, team, or people around them providing resources and belief.

candidates.label: Awareness / alertness
candidates.definition: A propensity to notice and be sensitive to information, needs and novel combinations, so that one recognizes when a lucky moment is the time to act.
candidates.applies_when: The person describes noticing or recognizing that something was an opportunity or the moment to act, being 'alert' or 'open to the universe'.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Recognition is present but no action follows; the authors note awareness alone is not enough.

candidates.label: Self-efficacy and belief
candidates.definition: Belief in one's capability and in the idea that leads the entrepreneur to stay open to and pursue chance breaks.
candidates.applies_when: The account links lucky breaks to believing in oneself or the idea, trusting hunches, or 'believing so hard something would break'.

candidates.label: Agency: acting on the chance event
candidates.definition: Taking definitive action to seize an opportunity when a random event occurs; what matters is what you do with it.
candidates.applies_when: The person describes taking a leap of faith, executing, or acting quickly on an unexpected event or opening.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The person merely notices the opportunity without acting (awareness).

candidates.label: Perseverance amplifying luck
candidates.definition: Staying with a course despite difficulties so that a small initial bit of luck can be turned into something bigger over time, or so that luck eventually shows up.
candidates.applies_when: The account ties lucky outcomes to persistence, not giving up, or staying in the game long enough for a break.

candidates.label: Advancing venture success
candidates.definition: Perceived luck, in combination with structural and agentic factors, is seen as a critical determinant of venture success and reflects willingness to act.
candidates.applies_when: The entrepreneur credits luck with a share in venture growth or success or in enabling action despite uncertainty.

candidates.label: Choice-to-chance continuum
candidates.definition: Entrepreneurs vary widely in how much they credit luck, from 'not luck at all' to 'majority luck', often giving percentages or qualifications.
candidates.applies_when: The person states how much of their success was luck versus skill or hard work.

candidates.label: Luck as humility narrative
candidates.definition: Invoking luck may reflect genuine belief or serve as a narrative device to project humility to an audience.
candidates.applies_when: The person attributes success to luck in a self-deprecating way, possibly for an audience such as investors.

candidates.label: Retrospective reframing of bad luck
candidates.definition: Luck is judged post hoc; an event first seen as bad luck can later be reframed as good luck once capitalized on.
candidates.applies_when: The person narrates a setback that in hindsight they describe as fortunate for the venture.

candidates.label: Skill or unseen structure
candidates.definition: Outcomes attributed to luck may instead be due to skill, which is hard to distinguish from luck, or to unseen structural patterns misattributed as luck.
candidates.applies_when: An account where an event called lucky can be explained by expertise, market timing skill, or structural position.

candidates.label: Uncertainty vs luck
candidates.definition: Uncertainty is forward-looking doubt that delays action, whereas luck is a backward-looking attribution about what enabled action.
candidates.applies_when: The person discusses not knowing what would happen before acting, as opposed to explaining afterwards what went their way.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The person is retrospectively attributing an outcome to fortune.

candidates.label: Fostering conditions for luck
candidates.definition: Entrepreneurs cannot control luck events but can make themselves more open by being alert to connections between circumstances and people and confident in their capabilities.
candidates.applies_when: The person describes deliberately cultivating alertness, networks, or confidence so as to catch chance opportunities.
